plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. Bidding below value only risks losing profitable auctions, while bidding above value risks losses. With my value at $6, I'll bid exactly $6 to maximize expected profit—winning only when profitable (paying less than $6) and losing when the price would exceed my value.

This is a second-price auction where I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes my expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks overpaying. With no history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $40.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it doesn't matter what others bid, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks losing money. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $28 to maximize expected profit.
